correctness.rationale: The arrow-wise wedge rank condition follows by expansion of the commutator in \(\mathbb F_q Q/J^2\). Each arrow-vector fiber has \(q^t\) choices when endpoints agree and exactly q when different, in every characteristic and for every \(t\ge2\). Summing independent arrow constraints over vertex t-vectors yields the exact normalized Fortuin–Kasteleyn polynomial. For \(t>m\), the exponents \(t(i+j)-j\) for coefficients of \(Z_G(X,Y-1)\) cannot collide because their j difference is less than t; infinite prime-power evaluations identify the polynomial. The tree and cycle specializations were algebraically derived. Actual standalone direct-multiplication enumeration on eight small quiver/field pairs and one t=3 case matched independently computed state sums and printed VERIFY_OK. No finite test is used to infer a theorem over all fields or all graphs.

value.rationale: Exact pairwise commuting-tuple statistics of finite associative algebras are a natural invariant. The theorem classifies their dependence on arbitrary loopless quiver graph structure, proves orientation independence even with antiparallel arrows, distinguishes graph cycle structure beyond cardinalities, and determines when one fixed arity with all finite-field sizes recovers the entire ordinary Tutte polynomial. This is a meaningful infinite-family structural bridge, not an arbitrary finite slice or a synonym for existing Potts counts. The graph-side FK expansion, simple tree/cycle formulas, and old Kronecker pair count are acknowledged as already known. Limitations are finite loopless quivers with radical-square-zero relations, all field sizes for recovery and only the ordinary Tutte polynomial.
